react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on arachidonic acid metabolism and its branch eicosanoid synthesis as the dominant affected pathway in this treatment group. RaMP multi-DB ORA identified Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked hit with FDR = 2.1e-13 and a 1250-fold enrichment, driven by five input lipids: arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-prostaglandin J2, 5-HETE and 15-HETE. The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm independently returned Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as its top pathway (p = 0.0068) with a perfect 11/11 metabolite overlap, including all five driver lipids plus HPETE and EET intermediates that were not in the input list — demonstrating that the treatment perturbs the entire lipoxygenase and cyclooxygenase cascade feeding into these eicosanoid effectors. MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirmed Arachidonic acid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00590) as its top KEGG hit (p = 0.0396), with four of the five same driver compounds. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed zero structural conflicts across all five driver metabolites, ruling out any namespace artefact. The remaining four input metabolites — thiosulfate, methylmalonic acid, 5-androstenediol, and xanthine — did not achieve significant enrichment in lipid pathways and likely represent secondary or organ-specific perturbations. The convergent biological story is one of pharmacological or inflammatory modulation of the COX/LOX axis: arachidonic acid is mobilised from membrane phospholipids, shunted through 5-lipoxygenase toward leukotriene A4 and the HETEs, and through cyclooxygenase toward 15-deoxy-PGJ2, consistent with NSAID, cytokine, or oxidative-stress treatment effects.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on eicosanoid synthesis and arachidonic acid metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA identified Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked WikiPathways hit with FDR = 2.1e-13, driven by five metabolites: arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-PGJ2, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00590 (arachidonic acid metabolism) as the top pathway, matching the same four metabolites. The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm independently returned Arachidonic acid metabolism as its top pathway (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, p = 0.0057) with a perfect 11/11 metabolite overlap, including the same arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE as in the ORA hits. Pathway-membership verification via RaMP confirmed all five driver metabolites are canonical members of WP:WP167. The convergent biological story is pharmacological or inflammatory modulation of the COX/LOX axis: arachidonic acid (released from membrane phospholipids) is shunted through 5-lipoxygenase toward leukotriene A4 and the HETEs, and through cyclooxygenase toward 15-deoxy-PGJ2. Thiosulfate, methylmalonic acid, 5-androstenediol, and xanthine likely represent secondary or organ-specific perturbations not captured by the lipid-centred enrichment.

Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) is a substrate in Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) via ALOX5 (5-lipoxygenase) toward leukotriene A4.

Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) is a key driver of Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) with signal compounds arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-prostaglandin J2, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE through PTGS1 (COX-1) and ALOX5.

Leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909) is a key driver of Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) with signal compounds arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-prostaglandin J2, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE through ALOX5.

react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP-DB multi-database ORA returned Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked pathway with FDR = 2.1e-13, fold enrichment 1251, and five metabolites hit: arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-prostaglandin J2, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE. The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm on the human_mfn empirical network independently returned Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as its top-ranked hit (p = 0.0046) with a perfect 11/11 metabolite overlap including arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, and 5-HETE. A second mummichog network hit, Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate), captured 5 of the input metabolites and further corroborates the COX-branch activity. Cross-paradigm convergence on the arachidonic acid eicosanoid axis is therefore supported by both ORA (RaMP) and m/z network analysis (mummichog). The five driver metabolites are verified members of WP:WP167 via the RaMP metabolites_hit list. Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) is a key driver of eicosanoid synthesis through its conversion via PTGS1 (COX-1) to prostaglandin derivatives, and via ALOX5 (5-lipoxygenase) to leukotriene A4 and the HETEs. 5-Androstenediol (KEGG:C04295) was independently captured by mummichog C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis (p = 0.060) and androgen/estrogen metabolism (p = 0.070), indicating a secondary steroid axis perturbation. Thiosulfate, methylmalonic acid, and xanthine did not appear in any top-10 pathway hit and represent non-lipid background variation.
